title: On Grasping the rail with one hand
subtitle: 努力坚持 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 努力坚持（人与自我·做人与做事·努力与坚持）
meta: 主题语境：努力坚持（人与自我·做人与做事·努力与坚持）　|　核心词汇：grasp　|　正文 347 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 grasp 的形式与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1959 the musician ① grasped the rail with one hand at once, and every listener in the hall said it was the first time anybody had done such a thing there. Three nights on, people still spoke of how quietly it was done and of how, ever since, the musician ② grasps the rail with one hand in the rain without being asked. My mother said later that to ③ grasp the rail with one hand at all was the part nobody had expected.

By then somebody had surely ④ grasped the rail with one hand before — a line in the programme for December 1953 hints at it — but nobody could name the person. ⑤ Grasping the rail with one hand at once, the musician said once, is nine parts patience and one part nerve; it is not the doing of it that people remember.

My uncle, who kept the score at the far piano, meant the other thing entirely. He said that if anybody should ever ⑥ grasp the point at the third reading in the rain, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again. The rule the old hands handed down was plainer still: ⑦ Grasp the point at the third reading at once and never mention it again.

By 1966 the whole business had shrunk to half a line in the programme, and a new listener from the next hall ⑧ grasps the point at the third reading at once every night without once asking what it had cost the first time. My mother, who had watched all of it from the piano, said nothing at all; she simply ⑨ grasped the rail with one hand again when nobody else would.

⑩ To grasp the rail with one hand, my mother said in 1971, is not one thing but two: what you do and what the hall remembers of it. She said the second half never grows lighter, and nowadays, whenever the hall forgets, somebody grasps the rail with one hand in the rain again and somebody must grasp the rail with one hand at once all over again.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. v. 抓住（一般过去式 grasped the rail with one hand：1959 年乐师头一回这样做，二话不说地）
B. v. 抓住（一般现在 grasps the rail with one hand：自那以后成了老习惯，不必有人开口）
C. v. 抓住（不定式 to grasp the rail with one hand：文中两处，一是母亲说的“难就难在……”，一是结尾那句格言）
D. v. 抓住（过去完成时 had grasped the rail with one hand：1953 年十二月的节目单上那行字之前就有人做过）
E. v. 抓住（动名词 grasping the rail with one hand 作主语：“九分耐心、一分胆气”那一句）
F. v. 领会（grasp the point at the third reading：should ever 之后的原形，指万一真要去领会读第三遍时领会了那意思）
G. v. 领会（grasp the point at the third reading：祈使句，转述老手们当年立下的那条规矩）
H. v. 抓住（后段两处：新来的听客照例 grasps the point at the third reading，而母亲又一次 grasped the rail with one hand）

answers.why: grasp 意为“抓住”，1959 年乐师二话不说地抓住一只手抓住栏杆，那是音乐厅里头一回有人肯这么做，故用一般过去式 grasped。
grasp 意为“抓住”，自那以后乐师淋着雨把这件事做了一遍又一遍，不必有人开口，故用一般现在 grasps。
grasp 意为“抓住”，母亲说的是“难就难在肯抓住一只手抓住栏杆”，此处为不定式 to grasp the rail with one hand。
grasp 意为“抓住”，节目单里 十二月 那行字说明早在 1966 年之前就有人抓住过，故用过去完成时 had grasped。
grasp 意为“抓住”，乐师说“抓住一只手抓住栏杆这件事是九分耐心一分胆气”，此处 grasping the rail with one hand 作主语。
grasp 意为“领会”，叔叔说的是“万一真有人去领会读第三遍时领会了那意思”，should ever 之后用原形 grasp the point at the third reading。
grasp 意为“领会”，老手们留下的规矩是祈使句：立刻领会读第三遍时领会了那意思（grasp the point at the third reading at once），以后再也不要提起。
grasp 意为“抓住”，新来的听客每个夜晚都照例领会读第三遍时领会了那意思，从不问头一回的代价，用一般现在 grasps。
grasp 意为“抓住”，母亲在无人肯做的时候又一次二话不说地抓住一只手抓住栏杆，用一般过去式 grasped 叙述。
grasp 意为“抓住”，结尾那句是母亲 1971 年的话：要抓住一只手抓住栏杆，其实不是一件事，而是两件事——你做的那一件，和音乐厅记住的那一件。

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 grasp 的 3 种不同形式（过去式、第三人称、-ing、不定式等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1959 the musician grasped the rail with one hand at once, and nobody in the hall forgot it.
Even now the musician grasps the rail with one hand in the rain whenever the hall asks.
Grasping the rail with one hand at once, my mother used to say, is nine parts patience and one part nerve.
If anybody should ever grasp the point at the third reading in the rain, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again.
A new listener from the next hall grasps the point at the third reading at once every night, asking nothing about the past.
When nobody else would, my mother grasped the rail with one hand again, and the hall remembered that half.
